notes:
This update replaces the approved legacy demand model with Demand V2 in mid-v1.1.0. The previous medium (0.59) assessment applied to the legacy CPV/CONAPO/Furness methodology. Please review the changed sources and modeling approach; this submission does not request a particular tier or inherit Cancún's answers automatically.

Demand V2 uses CPV 2020 urban-block employed-resident data and Marco 2020 geography for spatial distribution and placement. EIC 2025 municipal controls and weighted person microdata provide the 2025 population, employment and mobility reference. The modeled area is the retained map territory, rather than the full municipalities used for source controls.

Destinations use physical DENUE establishment locations and establishment size-band priors. The effective workplace mode is historical_fine_transfer: municipal SCIAN/size groups use historical CE reference-year 2023 employment intensities where supported, and retain DENUE priors for missing, suppressed, excluded or unsupported groups. These are estimated attraction weights, not measured current jobs at each establishment. The report does not identify a DENUE reference year; no new DENUE vintage is claimed.

Synthetic OD allocation uses municipal survey evidence as partial aggregate constraints, beta 0.12 as the requested reference (not a calibrated beta), connected permitted territories, and OSRM driving baselines. Final destination targets are normalized model weights, not observed workplace headcounts. University and airport demand is reserved within the traveler budget. Cohorts contain exactly 50 people, with an aggregate rounding increase of 519 travelers above the pre-cohort integer budget of 663,631, giving 664,150 exported travelers.

CPV suppression is handled with aggregate residual/capacity reconstruction and limited fallback estimates described in the build report. CPV residential detail remains a 2020 spatial baseline; the 2025 controls and commuting observations are municipal, not new block-level observations. No claim of observed block-to-establishment OD, exact establishment employment, automatic tier improvement, or new game compatibility is made.

The workplace-area answer refers conservatively to the municipal CE intensity controls. DENUE locations and size-band priors are per establishment; they do not make the final employment counts observed per establishment. The workplace-placement dropdown uses the closest available conservative category for fine workplace-type priors. Actual locations are geocoded DENUE establishments, rather than allocation across building footprints. Historical municipal SCIAN/size intensities and fallback priors estimate establishment attraction; they are not measured current per-establishment headcounts. Please correct the dropdown classification if a different rubric category applies.

The residence-area answer refers to the CPV 2020 block-level spatial baseline. Current EIC 2025 controls and partial mobility evidence are municipal. Suppressed/missing CPV values and whole-cohort grouping introduce modeled components, so the final 2025 origins should not be read as measured block counts.

The full build report remains available locally with source hashes, reconstruction details, workplace fallback accounting, cohort rounding, allocation diagnostics and routing provenance. A public copy can be supplied for review if requested.
